title: Stale jit binary misreads newer repo data instead of failing fast on format mismatch
description:
An installed `jit` binary older than the repository's data produces opaque, misleading failures instead of a version-mismatch diagnosis. The repository already carries a single `schema_version` in `index.json`; the guard extends that one marker so an outdated binary fails fast and legibly.

## Background

Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03, session 2). Two incidents in one session while dogfooding storage/validation changes:

1. After the live repo migrated `gates.json` -> `gates.toml`, the stale PATH binary failed every command touching the registry with "Failed to read file: .jit/gates.json" (exit 4) — nothing hinted that the data had moved on and the binary was behind.
2. After `invariants.toml` bindings moved to `@/rule/...`/`@/gate/...` addresses, the stale binary's string-matching drift check reported 4 phantom enforcement-drift findings on a perfectly green repo.

Both read as repo corruption or regressions; the fix each time was `cargo install --path crates/jit`. `index.json` already carries `schema_version`, but the gates-file relocation and the binding-format change did not bump anything a binary checks.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: a single repository-format version (the existing `index.json` `schema_version`, or a marker extending it) is the authoritative on-disk compatibility marker, and it is bumped whenever an on-disk layout or interpretation changes.
- [hard] REQ-02: on startup, a binary whose supported format version is lower than the repository's refuses to operate and emits a single-line, nonzero error naming both the repository's format version and the version the binary supports, instead of a file-read error or a wrong validation verdict. Covered by a test pairing a newer-format repo with an older supported version.
- [hard] REQ-03: a binary whose supported version is greater than or equal to the repository's operates normally; writing with a newer binary may migrate or bump the marker as today.

## Notes

Guard is a single version check, not per-store schema versions.
